overview: After 1.c4 Nf6 White plays 2.b4, grabbing queenside space and putting the bishop on b2. Black can take the b-pawn with ...e6 and ...Bxb4 or simply develop with ...e6 and ...d5. It is an irregular surprise weapon, and I am not sure of the exact theory.

white_ideas.idea: b4-b5 space gain on the queenside
Meet ...Bxb4 with a lead in development

typical_structures.structure: Flank pawn offer with c4 and b4 against a Nf6 set-up

character.notes: Unbalanced because White's b-pawn is loose, but little forced play.

gambit.notes: b4 can be taken by ...Bxb4 once ...e6 is played.

soundness.notes: Probably playable but not demanding; rarely tested at top level.

structure.notes: Flank opening with the centre not committed.

approach.notes: Rarely chosen by strong players, mostly a surprise.

level.notes: Few forcing lines; knowing the b4 pawn idea is enough.

character.reason: A flank opening with an offered pawn but little forced tactical play.

gambit.reason: The b4 pawn can be taken with ...Bxb4 once ...e6 is played.

soundness.reason: Not clearly refuted, though White's early pawn offer gets little back.

structure.reason: Neither side commits the centre pawns early.

level.reason: Few moves to learn, but a speculative line is not a first repertoire choice.

plans.reason: White fianchettoes on b2 and expands with b4-b5.
